idiom_name: readonly record struct Step + Func<Step> thunks driven by a while loop
implementation_notes: C# emits no tail call for ordinary mutual recursion even though the IL tail. prefix exists (the runtime offers it, the C# compiler does not use it here), so the trampoline is hand-written: a step type holding either the value or a System.Func<TResult> thunk, and a while loop that follows the thunks until the value appears. A record struct keeps the finish case allocation-free while the delegate still boxes its capture. Use it for deep parser or tree walks; for bounded depth a plain recursive method keeps readable stack traces and costs nothing.
pitfalls: Each thunk allocates a closure and its captured state; in hot loops the allocation dominates, so prefer threading an immutable state record through a delegate parameter instead of capturing locals.
Exceptions thrown by a step propagate out of the driver and the logical recursion frames are missing from the stack trace; record the step context in the step type if diagnostics matter.
Mixing async lambdas into steps turns the driver into an async state machine - keep a synchronous driver and an async driver separate rather than awaiting inside the loop.
